Application Areas: Development of high-efficiency, large-scale renewable energy sources (e.g., stable perovskite solar modules)
Creation of quantitative, imaging-based biomarkers for diagnosing and tracking the severity of neurological conditions like Degenerative Cervical Myelopathy (DCM) and "Long COVID"
Informing clinical decision-making, such as identifying candidates for surgical decompression in DCM and predicting post-operative recovery
Advancing basic neuroscience research by providing methods to study the high-speed (millisecond-scale) dynamics of spontaneous brain activity and resting-state networks
Assessing the functional integrity of specific neural pathways (e.g., sensorimotor spinal tracts) in patients with physical impairments who cannot perform standard voluntary motor tasks
Key Research Thinking Patterns: Bridging Spatiotemporal Scales: Connecting phenomena observed at one scale (e.g., fast, microscopic) to their emergent properties at another (e.g., slow, macroscopic). (e.g., Linking ultrafast, transient neural "co-activation patterns" (CAPs) in EEG (sub-100ms) to the emergence of slow, time-averaged resting-state networks (RSNs) and validating material modifications on small-scale solar cells (0.1 cm²) before scaling them up to large-area modules (1160 cm²)).

Quantitative-Clinical Correlation: Developing and validating objective, measurable data as biomarkers by correlating them with established clinical or functional performance scores. (e.g., Correlating Magnetization Transfer Ratio (MTR) in specific spinal tracts with mJOA motor scores in DCM patients and linking Default Mode Network (DMN) connectivity with RBANS cognitive performance scores in post-COVID patients).

Granular (Localized) Analysis: Moving beyond global or regional averages to isolate and analyze specific, high-resolution components where critical functions or failures occur. (e.g., Focusing on the perovskite/ETL interface as the key location for modification in solar cells, identifying tract-specific (not just regional) white matter damage in DCM, and analyzing segmental-level (C5-C8) functional activation in the spinal cord).

Adaptive Methodology: Modifying standard experimental techniques to accommodate the physical limitations of a subject or the chemical constraints of a material system. (e.g., Using passive median nerve stimulation for fMRI because DCM patients cannot reliably perform voluntary motor tasks and selecting a non-polar solvent (CB) to apply NFAs, which passivates defects without causing the structural damage that a traditional polar solvent (IPA) would).
Summary Description: Dr. Lei Ding specializes in a dual focus spanning Neuroscience and Materials Science. In neuroimaging, he investigates brain and spinal cord function, exploring functional connectivity (FC) in the Default Mode Network (DMN) for post-COVID cognitive complaints and using task-based spinal fMRI and tract-specific Magnetization Transfer Ratio (MTR) to assess Degenerative Cervical Myelopathy (DCM). He also develops advanced electrophysiology methods, using Independent Component Analysis (ICA) and k-means clustering on EEG data to define transient Co-Activation Patterns (CAPs) and their relationship to Resting-State Networks (RSNs). In materials science, he contributes to advanced photovoltaics, specifically enhancing inverted perovskite solar cells (i-PSCs) through top interface modification with N-type semiconductors to improve efficiency and stability.
